title: CORE EQ
summary: Core's EQ in its own window: up to eight bands drawn as hills over what comes in, each a bell, a shelf, a cut or a notch, on both sides, one side, the middle or the sides, and able to move with the level.
steps: Add CORE EQ to a track from the Effects menu, then Open. Play the song: the grey shape behind the curves is what comes into the EQ.

Each band has its own blue, from light to dark. Drag a point: left-right is the frequency, up-down the gain. The wheel over a point changes its Q. Double-click an empty place to add a bell there; double-click a point to turn its band off.

Right-click a point, or use its card, for the shape (bell, low or high shelf, low or high cut, notch), the slope of a cut (12, 24 or 48 dB per octave) and the channel (stereo, left, right, mid or side).
Dynamic: the band's gain moves by up to Range when that band is louder than Threshold. A dynamic cut of -4 dB at 3 kHz only cuts when the lead gets harsh. The dashed curve shows where it goes.
Auto Gain takes back the EQ's average boost or cut, so a louder sound does not fool you. A and B compare two settings; the LFOs move a band's frequency, gain or Q with the tempo.

examples.title: Clean the low end of a lead
examples.text: Band 1, a low cut at 200-300 Hz, 24 dB/oct: the lead leaves the room under it to the kick and the bass.

examples.title: Tame a harsh lead
examples.text: A dynamic bell at 3 kHz, Q 1.4, Range -6 dB, Threshold about -30 dB: it only cuts on the loud notes.

examples.title: Wider top, mono bottom
examples.text: A high shelf of +2 dB at 8 kHz on Side, and a low cut at 150 Hz on Side: the top opens out, the low end stays in the middle.

examples.title: Take out a ringing note
examples.text: A notch on the ring (find it by sweeping a narrow +12 dB bell, then change it to a notch).

styles.why: Tight low cuts on everything but the kick and the bass; dynamic bells on the leads keep them bright without hurting.
Cut the boxy 200-400 Hz on the bass tops and the mids of the pads, so the dark sounds stay clear.
A clean low end: a low cut on every track that is not the kick or the bass.
Gentle shelves: darker tops and a soft low end, the space stays wide on the sides.
